blind_target.authors: klein Selle, N., Verschuere, B., Kindt, M., Meijer, E. H., & Ben-Shakhar, G.
blind_target.title: Orienting versus inhibition in the Concealed Information Test: Different cognitive processes drive different physiological measures.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The present study intends to (1) provide a constructive replication of klein Selle et al. (2016) using the autobiographical CIT, and (2) extend their work by testing an additional prediction derived from orienting theory, using an item-salience manipulation.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The present study confirmed earlier findings by klein Selle et al. (2016) and revealed a fractionation between the different physio- logical measures.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall confirmation of the prior paper; the salience manipulation is an extension, and comparisons to other studies provide context.

luna_triage.reason: The present study explicitly conducts a constructive replication of Klein Selle et al. (2016)'s response-fractionation finding using an autobiographical CIT. The Results and Discussion report the corresponding SCR, respiration and heart-rate pattern and explicitly confirm the earlier findings. Reference 1847 is Riccelli et al. (2017), a distinct personality-neuroanatomy paper, so it does not represent the CIT original.
